declared_purpose: Provide an agent and standalone Bluesky/AT Protocol CLI for reading feeds, profiles, notifications and threads; publishing text and images; and managing engagement, follows, blocks and mutes. Entry requirements include checking authentication, using local hidden-prompt login, previewing drafts unless final text was supplied, verifying specified mutation targets, and requiring image alt text. Individual cached fields and repeated API lookups are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Specify agent authentication, preview and target-verification requirements
data_operations.data_scope: Account identity, draft text, selected account/post targets, and an app password entered locally rather than in chat
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local CLI and its caller; app-password entry is directed to the user's local hidden prompt
data_operations.condition: When following the skill; previews may be skipped when the user already supplied final text

data_operations.operation: Install and persist the runtime dependency
data_operations.data_scope: The atproto package requirement and installed runtime files; no account data is explicitly passed to pip
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: pip and its unspecified configured package source; scripts/venv
data_operations.condition: Wrapper execution when the virtual-environment directory does not exist

data_operations.operation: Read and rewrite local authentication configuration
data_operations.data_scope: The entire configuration JSON, including supported session and legacy credential fields
data_operations.condition: Authentication, identity checks, login, migration, refresh or logout; directory creation requests mode 0700 and file creation requests 0600, without resetting existing modes

data_operations.operation: Accept login credentials and obtain authentication state
data_operations.data_scope: Handle and app password; returned handle, DID and exported session string
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: atproto Client.login authentication boundary; returned handle, DID and session are saved locally, and identity is printed to the caller
data_operations.condition: Explicit login; getpass is used unless legacy --password is supplied. The command does not explicitly save the app password

data_operations.operation: Restore sessions, save changed sessions, and migrate legacy credentials
data_operations.data_scope: Stored session string, or legacy handle and app_password; newly exported session
data_operations.condition: Commands requiring a client. Session restoration takes precedence; successful legacy login deletes app_password from the rewritten configuration. Session restoration's network behavior is unresolved

data_operations.operation: Delete selected local authentication fields on logout
data_operations.condition: Only when a truthy session exists. This path makes no remote revocation call and does not remove app_password

data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the invoking caller
data_operations.condition: A stored handle triggers get_client; otherwise the command reports that the user is not logged in

data_operations.operation: Read selected image files and display local draft previews
data_operations.data_scope: Draft text, target references, detected URLs, image path, alt text, full selected image bytes and image size
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI process memory; preview text and metadata go to the caller through standard output
data_operations.condition: Post/thread image bytes are read before the dry-run branch and rejected above 1 MB. Dry-run paths return before get_client or posting calls

data_operations.operation: Resolve identifiers and construct link, mention and thread references
data_operations.data_scope: Target and mentioned handles, returned DIDs, post URIs, CIDs and reply-root references; URLs extracted from draft text
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: atproto get_profile/get_posts for resolution; derived identifiers and facets remain in process until used in a command
data_operations.condition: Post-reference resolution or actual posting with mentions. URLs become link facets; this source does not fetch their contents. These are identifier derivations, not demonstrated sensitive-attribute inference

data_operations.data_scope: Requested count and search query; returned post text, author identity, timestamps, identifiers and engagement counts
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Bluesky API through atproto get_timeline/search_posts; selected result fields return to the caller
data_operations.condition: Requested read command; JSON includes more structured identifiers than text output

data_operations.operation: Fetch notification activity and read status
data_operations.data_scope: Requested limit; notification reasons, author handles/DIDs, timestamps, URIs and isRead state
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Bluesky notification API through atproto; selected fields return to the caller
data_operations.condition: Notifications command; URI, DID and read status are included in JSON output

data_operations.data_scope: Requested handle or authenticated self; identity, biography, counts, and avatar/banner URLs for profile JSON
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: atproto get_profile; selected fields return to the caller
data_operations.condition: Profile or stats command; stats displays only handle and counts

data_operations.data_scope: Target URI and requested reply depth; returned posts, author identities, timestamps, counts and parent/reply relationships
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: atproto get_post_thread, with preliminary resolution for non-at:// inputs; output to the caller
data_operations.condition: Thread-view command; text traversal displays parents and replies, while JSON collects the target and replies

data_operations.operation: Submit public posts, replies, quotes and multi-post threads
data_operations.data_scope: Approved text and facets, optional selected image bytes and alt text, reply-root/parent or quoted-post URI/CID references
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Bluesky posting boundary through atproto send_post/send_image; intended remote post records; resulting URLs return to the caller
data_operations.condition: Validation succeeds and dry-run is disabled. Thread posts are submitted sequentially; a later failure leaves earlier successful posts without rollback

data_operations.source: Like, repost, follow, block and mute commands
data_operations.data_scope: Authenticated account context; target post URI/CID or account DID; block record includes a creation timestamp
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Bluesky engagement, graph and mute APIs through atproto; remote relationship or preference state
data_operations.condition: Requested mutation after target resolution; block creation checks existing viewer blocking state. CLI confirmation applies only to configured guarded commands

data_operations.operation: Request remote record or preference removal
data_operations.source: Delete, unlike, unrepost, unfollow, unblock and unmute commands
data_operations.data_scope: Post URI; authenticated account DID and relationship record key obtained from viewer state; target DID for unmute
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Corresponding Bluesky deletion/unmute APIs through atproto
data_operations.condition: Requested removal; relationship deletions check available viewer state. These calls do not establish erasure from server backups, caches or other recipients

data_operations.operation: Read optional mutation-confirmation settings and user input
data_operations.data_scope: BSKY_CONFIRM_MUTATIONS, --yes, target description and typed confirmation
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process and terminal/caller; no persistence is implemented
data_operations.condition: Guarded command calls this helper. Prompts occur only when the environment setting enables them and --yes is absent; noninteractive execution then refuses

data_operations.operation: Create test fixtures and capture local subprocess output
data_operations.data_scope: Temporary configuration directory, synthetic identity/session fixtures, and CLI version or draft-preview output
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Test temporary directory and test-process memory
data_operations.condition: Tests are run; the cited fixtures are synthetic, and cited subprocess paths invoke version or dry-run behavior rather than authenticated posting

potential_excess.data_scope: Legacy app_password and associated configuration identity fields
potential_excess.condition: Logout with a legacy configuration lacking session leaves the configuration unchanged; a mixed configuration retains app_password even when session is removed
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Logout should end locally stored authentication. Legacy migration compatibility explains reading the password before migration, not retaining it after explicit logout
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Clear supported local authentication state and report logout status
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove app_password and account/session fields on logout regardless of whether session exists
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep legacy migration available until logout; do not claim local deletion revokes remote credentials or securely erases old file contents

potential_excess.condition: Successful login writes did beside the required session
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Session persistence supports subsequent authenticated commands; a separate stored DID is an implementation choice
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain usable authentication and display/use the authenticated account DID
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit the top-level did field from new configuration writes and remove it during migration or cleanup
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue obtaining the DID from client.me.did, as identity output and record operations already do; this does not establish what identifiers the opaque session contains

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated disclosure of the same post URI and repeated retrieval of its post/viewer data
potential_excess.condition: Unlike and unrepost first call resolve_post, which fetches the post, then unconditionally fetch the same URI again
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Removing a relationship requires its viewer-state record URI; the second full lookup is potentially a redundant action rather than extra fields in the deletion request
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve the target and obtain a valid like/repost record key
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse the resolved post's viewer state when present and sufficiently current; make another lookup conditional on missing state or a deliberate freshness requirement
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep missing-relationship checks, target verification, confirmation behavior and any required post-confirmation freshness

potential_excess.data_scope: Preliminary full-post retrieval used only to obtain the target URI
potential_excess.condition: Thread view receives a URL or bare post ID; at:// inputs already skip this preliminary request
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Viewing the conversation requires get_post_thread; the preceding CID-oriented post fetch is a potentially redundant action
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Construct the correct URI, resolve a handle when necessary, and fetch the requested thread
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Separate URI construction from full-post resolution and call get_post_thread directly after constructing the URI
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve handle-to-DID resolution, self-account handling for bare IDs, requested depth and equivalent not-found handling

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated mention handles, and @-matching fragments inside URLs that become link facets
potential_excess.condition: Actual posting text repeats a mention or contains an @ fragment inside a URL; mention extraction runs separately from the URL-prioritized facet parser
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Correct mention facets require resolving genuine mentions; duplicate or unused resolutions are extra API actions
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve each genuine mention to a DID and retain correct URL facets
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the combined token parser to identify standalone mentions and resolve each distinct handle once per build
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve every displayed mention, existing unresolved-mention fallback, URL contents and facet offsets

potential_excess.data_scope: Entire selected image contents during preview or rejection of oversized files
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local CLI process memory; no remote image disclosure occurs on these dry-run paths
potential_excess.condition: Post or create-thread uses --image; read_bytes occurs before size rejection and dry-run return
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Preview and size validation need path, alt text and file size. Full bytes are extra local data in that validation step, although they are necessary for actual image upload
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Verify the selected file and size, show the same preview, and read image contents for a real upload
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check file metadata and reject oversized files before reading contents; defer read_bytes until an actual upload is requested
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain alt-text requirements, size/error reporting and upload-time size checks against file changes

unknowns: All supplied package files were reviewed. The atproto implementation and transitive dependencies are absent; exact network hosts, routing, authentication transport, session contents and session-restoration network activity cannot be established.

Image bytes are passed to send_image without package-level sanitization. SDK transformations, metadata retention and the exact uploaded representation remain unresolved; embedded metadata is not demonstrated.
Remote retention, logging, federation, visibility of individual relationship/preference types, and deletion or credential-revocation guarantees are not established by the supplied source.
pip's configured package sources, dependency behavior and external installation logging are unspecified.
Existing filesystem permissions, historical configuration copies and secure erasure are not established. Creation modes do not reset existing permissions.
SDK exception contents and any caller-side logging or retention of normal CLI output are unknown; returning output to the caller does not itself establish onward disclosure.
